newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wants to "refound" welfare - Veltroni.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wants to "refound" welfare - Veltroni.

text.p: Italian deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni was quoted as saying Italy's centre-left government wanted to "refound" the welfare state rather than simply slash spending.

"Until now the right has only seen the problem in terms of cutting the welfare state. We want to refound it. There is a world of difference in between," Veltroni told Rome daily La Repubblica in an interview.

Veltroni reiterated his call for root-and-branch reform of the welfare system and said the government should sit down with unions and business leaders after the 1997 budget had been approved by parliament.
He said the government wanted to achieve reforms through dialogue with the unions rather than confrontation.
An attempt by former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi to push through a major pensions reform in 1994 was dropped in the face of strong opposition from the unions.
"The difference between us and Berlusconi is that when the unions went on strike he said they should think of working, while we want to sit down with them around a table," said Berlusconi.
"The problem is not to reduce social spending, it's to bring it back into balance and make it more productive," said Veltroni.
Fiat honorary chairman Giovanni Agnelli and Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio both called on Monday for action to reform the welfare state.
